chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made it upon himself to walk to the Sacred House of God, and for every slave he owned to be free if he went out with his aunt to Mecca, and he did not hire a mount for her nor did he accompany her. He said: 'It is not valid; he should hire a mount for her and he should go out with her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a conditional vow to walk to Mecca if slaves are freed?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a conditional vow to walk to Mecca while freeing slaves is valid but requires the vow-maker to ensure his aunt is properly accompanied, either by hiring a mount for her or traveling with her. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly principle that vows (nadhr) are not absolute if they conflict with established social obligations (mustahabbat or wajib) like kinship ties (silat al-rahim) and proper care of family members. It underscores that fulfilling a vow must be done in a manner consistent with ihsan (excellence in conduct) and does not exempt one from familial duties.
